name: Ramchi
description: Ramchi is a partition card game for 3 players. Each player forms up to five combinations of three cards (trips, straight flush, straight, flush, unrelated). Players compete round by round; winner of round N wins N chips from each opponent. Four of a kind wins the hand immediately. Target: most chips.
origin: Pakistan (popular among Afghan refugee communities); variant of Afghan Chor Voli

history.origins: Ramchi is a partition card game in the same family as the Afghan game Chor Voli. Chor Voli was learned by Gyula Zsigri from Sherzod Lukmoni in 1992. Ramchi was described in 2011 by Tilman Schieber as popular in Pakistan among Afghan refugee communities; it uses three players and 17 cards each, with up to five 3-card combinations and a distinct straight ranking (A-2-3 highest, 2-3-5 ramchi second).
timeline: 2011: Ramchi described by Tilman Schieber as popular in Pakistan among Afghan refugees.

setup.players: Three players (or four in a variant with 13 cards each and up to four combinations).
setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack (international pattern). Fifty-one cards are dealt in Ramchi: 17 each to three players, with one card placed face up; the holder of the two of diamonds may exchange it for the face-up card.
setup.dealing: 17 cards each; 1 card placed face up. Holder of 2♦ may exchange it for the face-up card. Four of a kind wins the hand immediately with no play.

rules.objective: Win the most chips. Form 3-card combinations; win rounds; round N pays N chips.
rules.gameplay: 1. Check for four of a kind (instant win). 2. Form up to 5 combinations: trips > straight flush > straight > flush > unrelated. 3. Discard at least 2. 4. Player to dealer's right leads; anticlockwise. 5. Each plays highest combo; highest wins round. 6. Round 1 = 1 chip, round 2 = 2 chips, etc. 7. Winner of round leads next. 8. Players with no combos sit out.
keyRules: Combinations: trips (AAA highest), straight flush (Ramchi = A-2-3 same suit), straight, flush, unrelated.
Round N winner collects N chips from each opponent.
Four of a kind wins whole hand.

strategy.basic: Maximize strong combinations; discard weak cards.
tips: Save Ramchi (A-2-3 flush) for later rounds.
